newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian gas reform body sets end-1997 timetable.
newsitem.headline: Australian gas reform body sets end-1997 timetable.

text.p: Australia's official gas reform group on Tuesday gave itself a new deadline of end-1997 for laying the foundations for a national gas market.
The Gas Reform Implementation Group, which wants to ensure gas can be traded freely over monopoly-owned gas pipelines, said it aimed to finalise a national access code by end-1997.
The group's chairman, Jon Stanford, made the announcement at a gas reform conference in Melbourne.
An industry access code is essential for the development of a national gas market, where gas can be traded freely and fairly across state and territory borders.
The reform process has missed its original deadline of July 1 last year, with participants unable to agree on a code amid concerns growing that the reform process is stalled.
Stanford said the issues to be resolved were complex, but they were at last close to being resolved.
"I would like to stress that the reform process has not been straightforward, but we are making significant progress," he told the conference.
"I am confident that in the very near future we will have a best practice national third-party access regime for gas pipeline systems across Australia."
